title: Control plane: GuardrailPolicy schema + versioned storage (+ migration for existing Optimize configs)
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Goal
Build the versioned GuardrailPolicy schema and storage layer in the control plane so Optimize ‘apply’ can reference a single, auditable source of truth for gating requirements. Include a migration plan for existing Optimize configurations so we can roll out gating in observe-only first without breaking current flows.

Context
Optimize can propose cost-saving config deltas (batching/caching/quantization/routing) that may regress output quality. The gating enforcement point is the control plane. This ticket establishes the durable policy representation: how thresholds are expressed, how versions are pinned, and how existing configs map into the new model.

References
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/optimize-quality-guardrails-gating-prd.json
- ADR (enforcement point): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-optimize-gating-enforcement-point.json
- ADR (threshold schema + versioning): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-threshold-schema-and-versioning.json
- Draft schema (Drive): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/guardrails-config-schema-draft.json

Deliverables
1) Data model + API
- New versioned resource: GuardrailPolicy
  - CRUD endpoints in control plane API
  - Explicit versioning semantics (immutable versions; create new version on change)
  - Retrieval by (tenant_id, policy_name) with latest + pin-to-version support
- Storage
  - Persistence table(s) with tenant scoping
  - Server-side validation (schema + referential checks)
  - Migration tooling + backfill script(s)

2) Schema requirements (v1)
- Must support policy selection by:
  - optimization_type: quantization | batching | caching | routing
  - model_family / model_id (allow wildcard)
  - workload tags (chat/tool-calling/structured-output/embeddings as applicable; allow customer-defined tags)
  - route_id (optional; guardrails differ by endpoint SLO)
  - customer tier (hosted vs dedicated vs private; and/or plan tier)
- Must define gating requirements:
  - required eval suites (identifiers)
  - metrics + thresholds
  - statistical guardrails: min sample size, CI rule, allowed delta
  - timeout behavior (block vs manual approval vs allow with audit flag) — per tier, but actual enforcement implemented in ENG-3913
- Must support pinning to artifact revisions:
  - prompt_set_revision (required for determinism when evaluating)
  - threshold_spec_version (string) to decouple schema from thresholds content
- Must support a safe “observe-only” mode toggle at the policy level (for rollout) while preserving auditability.

3) Migration plan for existing Optimize configs
- Today: Optimize configs stored per tenant/route with optimization settings but no explicit guardrails.
- Target:
  - Default GuardrailPolicy seeded per environment (staging/prod) for each tier
  - Existing tenants/routes get mapped to a default policy reference (policy_name + version)
  - No behavioral change at first: policy stored + surfaced in audit events, but gating enforcement remains off (observe-only) until feature flags enable it (ENG-3926/PR).

Migration steps
A) Schema + storage shipping (this ticket)
- Add GuardrailPolicy tables + API (disabled by default for UI).
- Seed baseline default policies (read-only) for:
  - hosted/self-serve
  - dedicated
  - private
- Add policy reference fields to OptimizeConfig entity (or equivalent control-plane config record):
  - guardrail_policy_name
  - guardrail_policy_version
  - guardrail_mode (optional: inherit/observe-only/enforce; if present, must be audited)

B) Backfill
- One-time backfill job:
  - For each tenant/route with OptimizeConfig: set guardrail_policy_name/version to default for its tier.
  - Record audit event: “OptimizeConfigGuardrailsBackfilled” (metadata only; no enforcement).
- Verification query + dashboard hook (counts by tier, missing policy refs).

C) Compatibility
- Ensure older Optimize clients/services can ignore new fields.
- APIs must be backwards compatible: if no policy reference exists, server resolves to default policy and returns it (read path) but does NOT persist unless requested (prevents surprises).

Acceptance criteria
- GuardrailPolicy schema validated server-side; invalid payloads rejected with actionable error messages.
- Create policy v1, then update by creating v2; v1 remains retrievable and immutable.
- OptimizeConfig can be updated to reference a GuardrailPolicy name+version.
- Backfill script tested in staging with rollback plan.
- Audit log fields are in place to support later tickets (ENG-3918), at minimum: who created/updated a policy version and what changed.

Non-goals
- Implementing gating decision logic (ENG-3913 / ENG-3914 / policy engine work).
- Building Console UI for editing policies (future; initial edits via API/admin tooling).

Open questions
- Do we model “thresholds” inline in GuardrailPolicy, or reference a ThresholdSpec object (separate versioned resource)? Current plan: inline for v1 with threshold_spec_version string for future extraction.
- How should per-tenant overrides be represented: separate policy version vs override layer? Current plan: per-tenant policy versions (copied from default) to preserve explicit auditability.

Implementation notes
- Prefer a canonical JSON schema with strict field ordering normalization to avoid non-deterministic diffs in audit logs.
- Policy names should be stable identifiers (e.g., “default-hosted”, “default-dedicated”, “default-private”) with versions as integers.
- Add server-generated ‘policy_uid’ for internal joins; keep (name, version, tenant_id) unique.

Risks
- Cardinality explosion if we allow unrestricted per-route policies; mitigate by encouraging per-tier defaults + limited scoped overrides.
- Migration/backfill could accidentally flip enforcement if flags are misconfigured; ensure mode defaults to observe-only and is not coupled to enforcement flags.

Rollout
- Stage 1: ship schema + APIs + seeds in staging; run backfill; verify via queries.
- Stage 2: ship to prod behind admin-only endpoints; run backfill in a maintenance window.
- Stage 3: enable observe-only logging (ENG-3918) before any enforcement.
comments: 2025-01-10 (Jordan Lee): Please ensure versioning semantics are immutable; policy evaluation depends on pinning. Also, include prompt_set_revision in the stored policy even if enforcement is later. If we allow ‘latest’, it must be explicitly requested by the caller (avoid silent upgrades).

2025-01-12 (Aditya Rao): For migration, we need a clear story for existing Optimize customers: no UI change at first, but audit logs should show guardrails policy attached even in observe-only. Please add a field we can expose later in Console without renaming.

2025-01-14 (Naomi Feldman): Security note: policy edits should be admin-scoped; include created_by/updated_by and retain history. We’ll likely need exportability later, so keep payload size bounded and avoid storing prompt contents here (only revisions/ids).

2025-01-16 (Benji Okafor): Drafted DB schema proposal: guardrail_policies (tenant_id, name, version, blob_json, created_at, created_by, checksum). OptimizeConfig gets guardrail_policy_name/version nullable. Will share PR for review.

2025-01-20 (Sean Gallagher): For backfill, we need a dry-run mode and metrics emitted: tenants_total, tenants_backfilled, missing_tier_mapping, failures. Also propose we tag the backfill job with a change window id for later incident correlation.

2025-01-22 (Michael Nguyen): Implementation underway. APIs implemented locally; working on migration scripts + staging seed data. Next: add server-side JSON schema validation + canonicalization to avoid spurious diffs.
